reason: The cited evidence (E2, E3) shows higher creep activation energy in HfTaTiVZr and TaTiVWZr HEAs vs. pure W, attributed to severe lattice distortion and dislocation interactions, but does not directly link this to enhanced tensile ductility, multi-slip activation, or fracture toughness. E1 only describes a pre-cracking method for pure W and provides no support for the alloy's properties or the proposed mechanism. Thus, the core mechanistic link from lattice distortion to improved plastic strain and toughness is largely unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Severe lattice distortions in multi-principal-element alloys increase dislocation pinning and promote multi-slip
These lattice distortions increase activation energy for dislocation motion relative to pure W
Increased activation energy and multi-slip lead to homogeneous plastic flow and delayed crack propagation
The equimolar WTaTiVZr alloy is a homogeneous single-phase BCC solid solution with severe lattice distortions
The proposed mechanism will enhance plastic strain and fracture toughness over pure W at 400–700 °C
